defensive.label: Defensive
defensive.fits: money you may need within a few years, or a fall that would make you sell

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.fits: money you will not need for years, and a fall you would wait out

opportunity.label: Opportunity
opportunity.fits: a long horizon, a fall you would buy into, and the knowledge to match

first_step_starter.label: First-step starter
first_step_starter.who: starting out: a student or in a first job, with a small amount and a long time ahead
first_step_starter.goal: start, learn and build the habit
tips: A savings buffer comes before the first euro invested

goal_builder.label: Goal builder
goal_builder.who: employed, often renting, saving for a home and for the long term at the same time
goal_builder.goal: a home deposit in 2 to 5 years, and long-term wealth
tips: The home money moves to safer ETFs as the purchase date nears

self_directed_trader.label: Self-directed trader
self_directed_trader.tagline: Your picks, on a solid core.
self_directed_trader.who: already invests alone, often at a neobroker or in crypto, and wants control and low costs
self_directed_trader.goal: control, low costs and fast gains
tips: Your risk level follows the loss you can bear, not the one you would like to take

cautious_saver.label: Cautious saver
cautious_saver.who: has savings and has never invested, for fear of losses and of mistakes
cautious_saver.goal: children, a buffer and a later pension
tips: Go in step by step over 6 to 12 months

late_starter.label: Late starter
late_starter.who: 45 or older with larger savings, starting late to close a pension gap
tips: Plan sales around the yearly EUR 10,000 capital gains exemption

quiz.text: A 3x leveraged ETF on an index. The index falls 10% in a day. Your money in the ETF...
Why is a leveraged ETF not made to be held for years?

choices.label: It resets every day, so over months it drifts away from 3x the index
It is taxed more when held

quiz.text: Bitcoin fell about 75% from its 2021 peak to its 2022 low. Can that happen again?

choices.label: Yes, crypto can lose most of its value
No, an ETF makes it safe

etf.title: What an ETF is
text: An ETF is a fund you buy on the stock exchange, like a share.
One ETF holds many companies at once: an MSCI World ETF holds about 1,400 large companies in 23 countries.
Its yearly cost is low, often 0.1% to 0.3%.
etf.question: You buy EUR 100 of an MSCI World ETF. What do you own?

choices.label: A small slice of about 1,400 companies
Shares of the company that sells the ETF

spread.title: Why spreading your money lowers the risk
text: If all your money is in one company and it fails, you lose everything.
In a fund of hundreds of companies, the same failure costs a fraction of a percent.
Spreading also across regions and kinds of assets (shares, bonds, gold) smooths the ride further. It lowers the risk of a big loss; it does not stop every dip.
spread.question: Which is riskier?

choices.label: All my money in one company
The same money in a world ETF

time.title: A monthly plan, and why time does the work
text: Investing the same amount every month buys more units when prices are low and fewer when they are high.
Over long periods, gains earn gains of their own: compounding.
Example, not a promise: EUR 50 a month for 20 years is EUR 12,000 put in. At 5% a year it would become about EUR 20,500.
time.question: Prices fall while you invest EUR 50 every month. Your EUR 50 now buys...

two_pots.title: Two pots: the home money and the long-term money
text: Money you need in 2 to 5 years should not ride the stock market: a fall just before you buy can cost part of the deposit.
Keep it in a safe pot (savings, short bonds) and invest only the long-term pot in ETFs.
two_pots.question: You buy a flat in 3 years. Where does the deposit go?

choices.label: A safe pot: savings or short bonds
An equity ETF, it grows more

fall_before_buy.title: What a fall means a year before you buy
text: Shares can lose a fifth of their value in a few months, and take years to recover.
Over 15 years that hardly matters. One year before you buy a home, it can cost part of the deposit.
That is why the home money moves to safer ETFs as the date nears.
fall_before_buy.question: Why move the home money to safer ETFs as the date nears?

choices.label: So a late fall cannot eat the deposit
Because the bank asks for it

costs.title: How the costs of a fund add up
text: A fund takes a yearly fee from its value (the TER).
Example: at 5% a year before costs, a 1% fee takes about a sixth of what you would have after 20 years. A 0.2% fee takes about 4%.
costs.question: Two world ETFs on the same index: one costs 0.2% a year, the other 1%. Over 20 years...

choices.label: The cheaper one keeps more of the gain

read_sheet.title: Read an ETF sheet: trend, macro and news
text: Trend: is the price above its average, and is the return positive?
Macro: does today's economy help or hurt this ETF? News: what our analyst reads for the next few days, with the other side of the argument.
None of them is a forecast to bank on. Together they tell you what the market is doing now.
read_sheet.question: The trend is up, the news leans negative. What does it tell you?

choices.label: The signals disagree, so neither is certain

leverage_crypto.title: Leverage and crypto: what can go wrong
text: A 3x leveraged ETF moves three times the index each day, and resets every day: in a choppy market it loses value even if the index ends flat.
Bitcoin fell about three quarters from its 2021 peak to its 2022 low.
Keep them small, and only with money you could lose.
leverage_crypto.question: An index gains 10%, then loses 10% the next day. A 3x ETF on it ends...

core_satellite.title: Core and satellites
text: Keep most of your money in a broad core (world shares, bonds) and your own picks in satellites: about a third, or less.
If a pick goes wrong, the core carries you.
core_satellite.question: Your theme ETF doubles and becomes half of what you hold. What has changed?

choices.label: My risk: I now depend on one theme

falls_pass.title: What a fall looks like, and why it passes
text: World shares fell by a third or more three times since 2000: in 2000-03, in 2008 and in 2020.
Each time they recovered: once in months, once over many years.
Selling in the fall turns a loss on paper into a real one.
falls_pass.question: Your ETF falls 20%. If you sell now...

inflation.title: Savings account or ETF: what inflation does
text: With prices rising 2% a year, EUR 10,000 kept at 0% buys about EUR 8,200 of today's goods after 10 years.
An ETF can lose value in a given year, but over long periods shares have beaten inflation.
That is why a buffer stays in savings and long-term money is invested.
inflation.question: Prices rise 2% a year and your savings earn 0%. After 10 years your money...

step_by_step.title: Going in step by step
text: Investing a large amount in parts, over 6 to 12 months, means a fall just after you start hurts less.
It may earn a little less if markets rise meanwhile, but it is easier to live with.
step_by_step.question: Why go in step by step?

choices.label: A fall just after the start hurts less

pension_gap.title: The pension gap in your own numbers
text: The legal pension often pays well under your last salary.
The gap is what you fill yourself: the earlier you start, the more time works for you.
pension_gap.question: You start 10 years later. To reach the same amount you must...

tax_sell.title: Tax when you sell, and the yearly exemption
text: In Belgium, gains on shares and ETFs are taxed when you sell, with a first slice of gains exempt each year (EUR 10,000 in our example).
Spreading sales over several years can keep more of the gains under the exemption.
Tax rules change: check the current ones with an adviser.
tax_sell.question: You have EUR 18,000 of gains. Selling half this year and half next year...

choices.label: Can keep both halves under the yearly exemption

pension_saving.title: Pension savings and ETFs side by side
text: Belgian pension savings give a tax reduction each year, up to a ceiling, and the money is meant to stay until your pension.
ETFs give no tax reduction, but you can sell them any time.
Many use both: pension savings up to the ceiling, then ETFs. Check the current ceilings with an adviser.
pension_saving.question: What does pension savings give that an ETF does not?

choices.label: Money I can take out any time
